newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK equity bears ambushed by shares surge.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK equity bears ambushed by shares surge.

text.p: UK equity options traders were caught wrong-footed by a surge in the London stock market on Tuesday after they took bearish positions in the belief that share prices would be depressed ahead of Wednesday's budget, dealers said.
Bid rumours resurfaced in National Westminster Bank after one trader had sold around 1,100 July 850 call options in the bank.
If this was an uncovered position -- one in which the shares are not held -- losses will arise as the stock rallies because call options will be worth more.
But if the trader also owned NatWest shares the profit from a stock price rise will be eroded by the short calls as the shares race up.
By 1300 GMT, NatWest shares had jumped up 36p to 843-1/2p.
Remaining with the banks, Abbey National was singled out for a bear call spread involving the sale of 1,000 July 850 calls at 12p and buying 1,000 July 950 calls at 2p making a net credit of 10p.
This credit would be the maximum profit from the deal if the shares stay below 850p at expiry because both calls will then be worthless.
But Abbey National shares were up 12-1/2p to 832-1/2p.

Over in FTSE 100 index options bearish traders were mauled as the futures market turned against them. One large deal was from a buyer of 1,000 July 4050 puts at 3p. Another was to buy 500 August 4700 puts at 140p.
One trader bought a put spread by selling 350 July 4650 puts and selling 350 July 4625 puts for 17p debit and will make a maximum of 8p profit if the market goes below 4625 at expiry.
By 1300 GMT, cash FTSE was up 66.8 at 4671.4 and September futures were up 105 points at 4711.
